quick-summary.why: Yes Madam is a Java + Spring Boot microservices architect seat, so the summary now leads Java/Spring Boot straight into 'Decomposed a monolith into 10-15 microservices' - the JD's single loudest requirement. The Amura detail sentence (causal inference, leakage-safe machine learning, 9-10 years of patient history, self-hosted models) was cut and replaced with the chat-platform stack the JD actually asks for: high-concurrency Go, two-stream Amazon Kinesis, multi-availability-zone failover and disaster recovery, Kubernetes and Terraform adopted company-wide. Amura survives as one compressed clause so the ten analytics/AI services still back the headline's AI claims and the JD's 'Exposure to AI/GenAI-enabled applications' good-to-have.
quick-summary.heads_up: The high-availability clause is scoped to the CHAT PLATFORM only - it never touches Amura, and the corpus names no broker there. The certification that drove it is deliberately unnamed in both the summary and VoltusWave bullet 3, because which certification is still an open question. Do not let anyone write HIPAA or ISO 27001 into it. Note the adjacency risk: the Business & Delivery skills block says 'ISO 27001-Certified Environment' and the Deque CI/CD bullet says 'achieving ISO 27001' - both are true and both are Deque, but be ready to say out loud that the VoltusWave certification is a separate, unnamed one.
quick-summary.hygiene: SaaS, SSO, AWS and AI all expanded on first use here, ahead of every later section. 'Decomposed' echoes 'decomposition' in the Deque and Rocket bullets - a mid-text noun echo, not a leading-verb collision. 'Cut infrastructure cost 25-30%' is unchanged from the master and keeps 'Cut' as Teletext's leading verb clean.

quick-vp.why: Cut 10 bullets to 7 and re-vectored to platform engineering, dropping every Amura AI bullet (RAG pipeline, adversarial self-review, confounder-gated cohorts, relapse model, protected health information in the VPC) and the patient-onboarding bullet. What is here maps one-to-one onto the JD: Kinesis two-stream = event-driven/messaging (and the honest answer to its Kafka good-to-have); Go at 100,000 concurrent = high traffic and high concurrency; the new Fortified bullet = 'Experience designing high-availability and high-performance systems'; the new Reimagined bullet = 'database performance, indexing, caching, optimization'; Datadog = the whole Observability section; the new Provisioned bullet = 'Docker and Kubernetes' plus cloud-native modernization and cost efficiency; the new Brokered bullet = 'define and drive technical standards' and 'influence technical decisions'.
quick-vp.heads_up: THREE NEW FACTS LAND HERE, all user-confirmed 2026-08-25 and none of them previously on any résumé. (1) The Fortified bullet is the high-availability design - multi-availability-zone, failover, disaster recovery - and it is scoped to the CHAT PLATFORM alone. Never let it migrate to Amura. The driver stays 'a certification requirement' because which certification is open; do not guess. (2) Kubernetes and Terraform were adopted as a COMPANY-WIDE STANDARD, not merely run, which is why the Provisioned bullet says 'making Kubernetes and Terraform the company-wide standard' rather than listing them as tools. (3) The Reimagined bullet's 'P95 under 30 ms at 100,000-user load' comes from the live card and is user-confirmed accurate - it is NOT the flagged '500 to 100,000 concurrent users' wording, which appears nowhere. The Scaled bullet is the master's exact wording, untouched, because the 100,000-concurrent framing is on the confirm-or-reject list. Expect 'walk me through the graph neural network architecture' regardless - it is still word four of the headline even though no VoltusWave bullet backs it on this version.
quick-vp.hygiene: 7 bullets, all 25 words or fewer (22/25/24/22/21/24/17), each with bold and a number or scale marker, no trailing periods. Four leading verbs are new and every stem was grepped across the whole file including the five card-only pre-2016 roles: Fortified (forti - 0 prior hits), Reimagined (imagin - 0), Provisioned (provision - 0), Brokered (broker - 0). Architected, Scaled and Deployed are the master's, kept in place per Rule 7. ECS is used short here because the Engineering Excellence block expands it first.

Four bullets are new to any résumé: Exposed (shared platform APIs, 20+ enterprise clients, API versioning, backward compatibility - the JD's 'REST APIs and API design principles' and 'define and maintain standards for API design'); Modernised (Jenkins to GitHub Actions, ISO 27001, 50% faster releases - 'CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices' plus the security-and-compliance good-to-have); Slashed (Puppeteer regression framework); Accelerated (time-to-market, 2+ weeks per sprint). Three existing bullets absorbed merge detail: Steered gained 'axe Monitor on Spring Boot 2.x and Java 8/17', Forged gained 'users, roles, clients, groups', Stewarded gained the 3-4 hours of daily backups and 40% fewer deploy errors.
quick-deque.heads_up: The 70-80% consolidation figure and 'approximately 300 enterprise instances' are both on the confirm-or-reject list and both are carried at their exact master wording - the Steered bullet only appends the stack after the figure, it does not restate the claim. The Puppeteer and Jenkins-to-GitHub-Actions bullets have never gone out before; be ready for detail questions on both. Java recency ends February 2025 and he shipped on Spring Boot 2.x, never 3.x - the résumé says 2.x plainly and should not be softened.
